original_value: An improved method of physical activity accelerometer data processing, involving a wider frequency filter than the most commonly used ActiGraph filter, has been shown to better capture variations in physical activity intensity in a lab setting. The aim of the study was to investigate how this improved measure of physical activity affected the relationship with markers of cardiometabolic health. Accelerometer data and markers of cardiometabolic health from 725 adults from two samples, LIV 2013 and SCAPIS pilot, were analyzed. The accelerometer data was processed using both the original ActiGraph method with a low-pass cut-off at 1.6 Hz and the improved method with a low-pass cut-off at 10 Hz. The relationship between the physical activity intensity spectrum and a cardiometabolic health composite score was investigated using partial least squares regression. The strongest association between physical activity and cardiometabolic health was shifted towards higher intensities with the 10 Hz output compared to the ActiGraph method. In addition, the total explained variance was higher with the improved method. The 10 Hz output enables correctly measuring and interpreting high intensity physical activity and shows that physical activity at this intensity is stronger related to cardiometabolic health compared to the most commonly used ActiGraph method.

result.paraphrase: A refined approach to processing physical activity accelerometer data, using a broader frequency filter than the commonly used ActiGraph filter, has been shown in a laboratory setting to better reflect changes in physical activity intensity. This study aimed to examine how this improved physical activity measure relates to cardiometabolic health markers. Accelerometer data and cardiometabolic health markers from 725 adults in two samples, LIV 2013 and the SCAPIS pilot, were analyzed. Data were processed with both the original ActiGraph method using a 1.6 Hz low-pass cutoff and the improved method using a 10 Hz low-pass cutoff. Partial least squares regression was used to assess the relationship between the physical activity intensity spectrum and a cardiometabolic health composite score. Compared with the ActiGraph method, the 10 Hz output shifted the strongest physical activity–health association toward higher intensities. The improved method also explained more variance overall. The 10 Hz output allows high-intensity physical activity to be measured and interpreted correctly and indicates that activity at this intensity is more strongly associated with cardiometabolic health than when using the most commonly used ActiGraph method.
